## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kosambiyajātaka* (Ja 428), also referred to as the *Kosambijātaka* [Anandajoti 2010], is a canonical birth story set at the Ghosita park (Ghositārāma) near Kosambī. According to the traditional framing, the Buddha delivered this teaching concerning the contentious, quarrelsome monks at Kosambī. Secondary scholarship notes that the account of the monks' dispute is derived directly from the Vinaya tradition [Burlingame 1921]. Within this instructional context, the text introduces the story of an executed neighbouring king whose prince chooses forbearance and reconciliation over retribution, framing moral admonitions on whether to wander with the wise or walk alone [Anandajoti 2010].
